newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia and Australia seek good relations.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia and Australia seek good relations.

text.p: Good relations between Indonesia and Australia were of benefit to both countries, the leaders of the two neighbouring states agreed on Tuesday.
Indonesia's President Suharto and Australian Prime Minister John Howard had 90 minutes of formal talks at the Freedom Palace in central Jakarta.
Howard arrived on Monday for his first official visit to Indonesia since taking office six months ago. He is due to leave for Japan on Wednesday.

"Both leader agreed there was a need for exchanges and visits betweeen officials, private businessmen and other members of society. Both leaders also mentioned the importance of media relations," State Secretary Murdiono told reporters after the talks.

"Both leaders agreed that good relation between Indonesia and Australia benefitted both sides. They also shared the view that meetings between them, like today's session, was very useful and should be continued in the future," Murdiono said.

Murdiono said Suharto had asked that Australia consider purchasing Indonesian-made planes. Indonesia currently builds light passenger aircraft and has a more ambitious project to build larger planes in the future.
Murdiono said the two countries had the potential to increase their trade. Indonesia is Australia's fastest growing market, and two-way trade in 1995-96 was worth A$4.2 billion (#3.3 billion).
Murdiono said Howard and Suharto also discussed the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) forum in Manila in November.
